tei:titleStmt.tei:title: אֲזַי בְּבׇגְדִי
Azai b-Vagdi — a seliḥah for 17 Tammuz (translation by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer)

tei:div.tei:head: Azai b-Vagdi — a seliḥah for 17 Tammuz (translation by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer)

tei:lg.tei:l: As I betrayed the words of my Dweller on High,
Bent in iniquity, my yoke from my rebuker heavied.
Gloating over me, the foe shocked me in a shock.
His wrath tore me and opposed me. (Job 16:9)
Deserting Their paths which were taught me,
Earned that Their roused at me wrath, rage, and anger.
Zealously, Their rage drawn, Their arrows shot at me.
And Their set me up to be Their target. (Job 16:12)
Hardships fivefold passed by me on this day,
Tearing my flesh, they set me as wastes.
Jaded and weary is my wearied soul,
Too knotted to hear, too disturbed to see. (Isaiah 21:3)
Cognizant of all these, I am awakened by groans.
Lapping flames burning my loins and kidneys.
Mourning I bitterly increase, distancing from joys.
For on this day, the tablets were shattered.
Nemesis mine, joined with his crowds, aimed at me,
Surrounding me like water, I drowned and none raised me.
On that, I wail in my mouth and persist in weeping,
For on this day, the daily-offering ceased.
Perforators overwhelmed me with a flowing stream’s force,
Exterminating me in a pit, giving me over as carrion,
Quoting a festival over me; my crowds were sore bereaved,
For on this day, an idol was set up in the Temple.
Rife-With-People the foe besieged, her entrances open wide.
Shot to waste was my vine on the day of rage and anger.
The foe saw their desire and his hand strongly overpowered.
For on this day Apostomus burned the Torah.
Evil gnashed teeth on the day the Cause’s wrath rose at me.
The foe and enemy had no mercy on elder or youth.
Their wrath burned at me, Their fires set me aflame.
For on this day, the city was breached.
Have mercy, Cause, and speak to the forlorn hearts,
On the seventeenth of the month sitting astonished.
Yah! Roll upon them Your many mercies from on high!
Deity, Sovereign, dwelling on the throne of compassion!

tei:note.tei:p: A poetic term for the people Israel
The opening line of the post-seliḥot recitation of the thirteen attributes of God.
